 Reporter banned from summit after asking Trump about Jensen Huang in front of Chinese leader 
 By 
 Steven Nelson 
 Published 
 Nov. 19, 2026, 6:48 a.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make New York Post a Preferred Source 
 SHENZHEN, China — A reporter in the White House press pool is in hot water with Chinese officials after shouting a question about ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang — who allegedly had an affair with a Chinese spy — during President Trump’s meeting with Xi Jinping.
 The Bloomberg reporter was blocked from attending the historic trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin because of the question she shouted out as Trump met his Chinese counterpart earlier Thursday, according to a pool dispatch .
 “President Trump,” the otherwise unidentified reporter had shouted, “has Jensen Huang been disloyal to the United States?”
 President Trump, left, and Chinese President Xi Jinping speak in Shenzhen, China, Nov. 16, 2026. Getty Images 
 Advertisement
 The Chinese delegate took offense at the question about the Nvidia CEO who resigned last week after admitting to having extramarital affairs — including with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang.
 A second reporter “started to ask a question but was shushed by Chinese officials,” the dispatch said.

 “The Chinese have passed along a message that yelling questions is considered extremely rude and we will be pulled from the room if we do so.”
 A White House official said they pushed to have the unnamed reporter reinstated, but Chinese officials stood by their decision.
 Huang has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month as pressure mounts on Capitol Hill to investigate his affair with Huang, who is not related.
 Huang and Tim Teter, Nvidia’s general counsel, are also slated to face questioning from three House committees on Dec. 1. It was not immediately clear when Huang’s Senate testimony will take place.
